sources.title: Andrew M. Childs, Lecture Notes on Quantum Algorithms (17 April 2025)
sources.locator: Complete 191-page PDF; full-document reading is inherited from the QA5 ledger; this batch inspected §4.3 (printed p.19), §19.3, and Hamiltonian simulation chapters 27 and 29.

contents.name: Chapter 4 §4.3, printed p.19: phase estimation
contents.reason: Supports the QPE Fourier/phase convention; the carrier checks the OP5 signed time scale and no-alias interval directly.

contents.name: Chapter 19 §19.3: amplitude amplification
contents.reason: Supports the two-dimensional rotation method; the finite random-iteration cap and failure bound are proved locally from current QA12 suppliers.

contents.name: Hamiltonian simulation chapters 27 and 29
contents.reason: Supports the distinction between supplied simulation access and its resource function; the carrier charges controlled, inverse, time, precision, and gate costs separately.

sources.title: Aram W. Harrow, Avinatan Hassidim, and Seth Lloyd, Quantum algorithm for linear systems of equations (arXiv:0811.3171)
sources.locator: Complete 15-page PDF; this batch inspected Appendix A1–A4, PDF pp.5–12, and the state-output/readout discussion in §§I–V, pp.1–15.

contents.name: Appendix A1, sine state (A1), U_invert steps 1–5, filter functions (A3), PDF pp.5–6
contents.reason: Supports the sine-window HHL route and filter conventions. OP5 table preparation, signed negative-QFT decoding, capped schedule, and all modified precision constants are specified and proved locally.

contents.name: Appendix A2, Theorem 1, Lemmas 2–3, PDF pp.7–10
contents.reason: The source motivates the Lipschitz and postselection arguments. The carrier independently proves its signed kernel moment, relative filter bound, OP5 error budget, and normalization constants.

contents.name: Appendix A3, sine-window Fourier calculation (A23)–(A32), PDF pp.10–11
contents.reason: Supports the exact finite sine-window Fourier kernel; the carrier derives the centered signed-label tail bound and its constant locally.

contents.name: Appendix A4, Hermitian embedding, PDF pp.11–12
contents.reason: Supports Hermitian dilation context; the carrier proves the rectangular spectrum, kernel, and pseudoinverse action from the current SVD and Penrose suppliers.

contents.name: Abstract and §§I–V, quantum state output and vector readout, PDF pp.1–15
contents.reason: Supports the state-output distinction; the lower bound on classical output length is proved by an explicit sign family.

sources.title: Andrew M. Childs, Robin Kothari, and Rolando D. Somma, Quantum algorithm for systems of linear equations with exponentially improved dependence on precision (arXiv:1511.02306)
sources.locator: Complete 31-page PDF; this batch inspected Problem 1 and Theorem 2, PDF pp.2–5, including the sparse/state-preparation oracle assumptions.

contents.name: Problem 1, sparse row/value oracle and Theorem 2, PDF pp.2–5
contents.reason: The source query statement is retained as a literature comparison and claim provenance only. It does not locally prove the required controlled sparse-simulation bridge for this OP5 access interface, so the item is owner-escalated.

contents.name: Problem 1 and input-state oracle, PDF pp.2–4
contents.reason: Supports the quantum state-output problem framing; the carrier explicitly defines the rectangular pseudoinverse target and its positive support gap.
